theorem.name: conjugate-sector response theorem
hypotheses: h is in Z3 and an involutive unitary or antiunitary symmetry Theta maps H_h to H_-h
the equilibrium or stationary state is mapped covariantly from rho_h to rho_-h
the real symmetrized probe vector transforms by a fixed real orthogonal parity matrix R
the probe convention and physical orientation are held fixed across sectors
theorem.response: C_h,ab = (1/2) Tr rho_h {Delta O_a, Delta O_b}
corollaries: If every retained probe has the same Theta parity, R=I or R=-I and C_1=C_2.
Every R-congruence invariant is equal in h=1 and h=2 even when the labelled matrices differ.
For one even and one odd probe, R=diag(1,-1); diagonal autocovariances are conjugate-sector even and the cross covariance is odd.
A single Theta-odd expectation value can separate h=1 from h=2, but a one-probe autocorrelation cannot because its parity is squared.

z3HarmonicDecomposition.evenMeaning: D_c compares the trivial sector with the conjugate-pair average and may be nonzero with exact CP/T symmetry.
z3HarmonicDecomposition.oddMeaning: D_s is conjugation/orientation odd and vanishes for same-parity probes under exact CP/T symmetry.
z3HarmonicDecomposition.protocolCorrection: The omnibus A_perp=sqrt(L(D_c)^2+L(D_s)^2)/S can be nonzero with D_s=0; it is a sector-dependence test, not by itself an orientation test.
recommendedReporting: the signed phase atan2(L(D_s),L(D_c)) after fixing orientation provenance

localityBoundary.pureFlatGaugeSector: Strictly local gauge-invariant operators made only from flat field strengths and local geometry cannot distinguish any h.
localityBoundary.chargedMatterEscape: A local charged field on a multiply connected space has a holonomy-dependent global state or spectrum, so a local density can acquire h-dependent expectation values through winding.
localityBoundary.qualification: After the charged field is integrated out, this dependence is nonlocal and generally gap/length suppressed; it is not a local derivative expansion reading flat curvature.

minimalEscapeLedger.target: separate h=1 from h=2 inside a positive symmetric response matrix
minimalEscapeLedger.minimumDatum: two probes of opposite CP/T parity and their cross response, or one even response multiplied by an independently sourced odd pseudoscalar

minimalEscapeLedger.target: derive a preferred orientation rather than merely measure one
minimalEscapeLedger.minimumDatum: microscopic CP/T breaking, an anomaly, an oriented boundary/history datum, or spontaneous breaking plus a recorded domain choice
minimalEscapeLedger.orientationImported: must be derived or independently evidenced
minimalEscapeLedger.a5Solved: only if the datum also acts covariantly on the internal family/chiral selector and passes the A5 gates

finiteToyModel.description: one charged particle on a three-site oriented ring
finiteToyModel.sectorFlux: Phi_h=2 pi h/3 with labels h=0,1,2 and h=2 represented as -1
finiteToyModel.symmetry: complex conjugation maps H_h to H_-h
finiteToyModel.localOddProbe: oriented bond current J_0=i t(exp(i Phi_h/3)|1><0|-h.c.)
finiteToyModel.response: thermal real symmetrized covariance Gram of (K_0,J_0)
expected: the spectra and every even thermodynamic scalar agree in sectors 1 and 2
the local current expectation reverses sign between sectors 1 and 2
all response matrices are positive semidefinite
the three labelled response matrices span three dimensions because the mixed-parity cross covariance supplies the odd direction
deleting the odd probe restores C_1=C_2
finiteToyModel.qualification: The ring is a logical counterexample showing that local charged observables can read globally prepared holonomy. It is not the programme's derived defect spectrum or an effect-size prediction.

exactClaims: Under the theorem hypotheses, same-parity real symmetrized response matrices satisfy C_1=C_2.
D_s=(C_1-C_2)/sqrt(3), so D_s is exactly the orientation-sensitive first-harmonic component.
D_c may be nonzero while C_1=C_2; a nonzero omnibus first harmonic does not prove orientation selection.
A two-probe positive Gram matrix needs opposite-parity probes for an odd cross-response direction without explicit symmetry breaking.
An externally oriented probe distinguishes sectors operationally but does not derive the A5 internal selector.
modelDependentClaims: The three-site ring realizes the exact symmetry pattern with a nonzero local current and mixed-parity covariance.
A gapped charged defect mode in the candidate programme could realize the same pattern if it is localized, anomaly safe and coupled to the declared probes.
speculativeClaims: The required oriented datum may descend from defect orientation, a parity anomaly, a CP-odd flavour invariant or cosmological/domain history.
Any such datum connects to A5 only if one action derives its coupling to the family/chiral sector rather than identifying two unrelated orientations by analogy.

protocolDecisions.evenAdvance: A_even nonzero with A_orient null establishes holonomy-sensitive response but not orientation or three individually readable sectors.
protocolDecisions.orientedAdvance: A_orient nonzero under a preregistered opposite-parity probe pair establishes oriented conjugate-sector readout after CP/T, calibration and order-reversal controls.
protocolDecisions.invalidInterpretation: Calling D_c-only response spontaneous orientation selection, or treating an apparatus loop direction as a derived A5 selector.
protocolDecisions.noGo: With pure flat BF, no charged winding sector, exact Theta symmetry and same-parity probes, all local readout routes to C_1 not equal C_2 are closed.
